rules.title: narrowing changes flow facts, not the declared semantic type
rules.contract: Normalize the declared domain once; an arm-local type is the declared domain intersected with Phi and structural coverage. No branch rewrites the declaration.

rules.title: closed-union exact alternative has one bounded elaboration
rules.contract: Inside a match-like refutable context whose subject is a normalized closed union, Identifier : TypeRef elaborates to UnionAlternativeBindPattern only when TypeRef is exactly one declared alternative identity; it performs UNION_INJECTION_TAG_TEST and binds that alternative. The existing `subject is Alternative` and adjacent `subject !is Alternative` comparison forms use the same exact-identity precondition and discriminator read but produce Bool and complementary Phi facts without binding. Everywhere else Identifier : TypeRef remains the irrefutable static TypedBindPattern.

rules.title: union alternative selection is not an open runtime type test
rules.contract: Pattern selection and `is`/`!is` read only the discriminator of the already-declared closed union and require one exact declared alternative identity. Subtyping search, reflection, provider lookup, Trait witness discovery, arbitrary downcast and refinement-predicate execution are forbidden.

rules.title: union formation requires a finite disjoint relation
rules.contract: After flattening and exact deduplication, every alternative pair must be proven DISJOINT by the finite R0 relation engine. EQUIVALENT or IMPLIES emits UNION_MEMBER_SUBSUMED; OVERLAPS or UNKNOWN rejects formation without inventing a runtime choice.

rules.title: refinement proof is required at every narrowing boundary
rules.contract: At construction, typed pattern, argument, return, and explicit cast boundaries, PROVED admits, DISPROVED emits the exact literal/range diagnostic, and UNKNOWN emits REFINEMENT_PROOF_REQUIRED. A boundary-free conversion emits REFINEMENT_IMPLICIT_NARROWING_FORBIDDEN.

rules.title: refinement operations have distinct outcomes
rules.contract: as? produces Option<T>; as! produces T with the declared failed-cast defect edge; T::check produces Result<T, error E>. None erases proof obligations or manufactures a Phi fact before success.

rules.title: def#guard narrowing requires one exact proof summary
rules.contract: A def#guard callable must be total, pure, terminating, nonsuspending, nonconsuming, authority-free and return exactly Bool. Narrowing requires a mandatory fresh GuardSummaryV1 in the finite normalized R0 calculus, exact direct callable selection, and stable actual places. The true edge receives substituted P and the false edge receives substituted not(P); opaque, missing, stale, indirect, wrapper, stored-Bool, or unstable-actual paths create no fact and never fall back heuristically.

rules.title: inline guards refine only an admitted structural partition
rules.contract: A guard runs after structural probe and before ownership commit. Only an inline finite R0 predicate may refine the true-edge Phi; a false guard commits no binding, move, borrow or authority.

rules.title: guarded arms are useful but never total coverage
rules.contract: Usefulness is checked against the structural partition, but guarded arms do not subtract from the exhaustiveness residual. A residual covered only by guarded arms emits MATCH_NONEXHAUSTIVE_AFTER_GUARDS.

rules.title: match usefulness and exhaustiveness are one ordered pass
rules.contract: For each arm compute structural coverage, diagnose an empty new set as MATCH_ARM_UNREACHABLE, subtract only unguarded coverage, diagnose otherwise after empty residual as OTHERWISE_UNREACHABLE, then emit MATCH_NOT_EXHAUSTIVE for a remaining witness.

rules.title: enum patterns resolve identity and payload before a guard
rules.contract: Resolve the VariantId in the subject Enum owner, then validate active payload arity, labels/positions and child pattern types. Unknown or foreign cases and inactive payload projections reject before guard evaluation and commit.

rules.title: or-pattern binders and ownership state must agree
rules.contract: Every alternative binds the same names with identical canonical type, mode, mutability, usable lifetime and capability. Projection path and source-field order may differ. Normally returning arms must join to the same usable-place state.

rules.title: probe and commit are transactional
rules.contract: Structural failure, an unreachable pattern, or a false guard produces zero committed bindings, moves, exclusive borrows and authorities; successful admission commits the precomputed plan atomically once.

rules.title: refinement shorthand preserves one explicit type boundary
rules.contract: `T where > rhs` inserts only the distinguished refinement subject `this`; `T in lower..upper` and `T in lower..<upper` normalize to one inclusive or upper-exclusive monotone interval. The bare spelling `T > rhs` is never a refinement because `>` retains its generic-close role. Shorthand normalization changes no proof obligation, evaluation, type identity, or runtime representation.

rules.title: a monotone chained binder Pattern binds and refines once
rules.contract: In a match Pattern owner, `lower <= name <= upper` and the corresponding monotone strict or descending spellings bind the subject exactly once to name, evaluate each bound at most once, and add the normalized chain fact to the arm-local Phi. Mixed directions reject before HIR, and the Pattern is not an implicit guarded arm.
